tender.title: DMNH 042 - LEVI Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure
tender.description:
Overview 
The purpose of this notice is to inform potential service providers of Shropshire Council’s intention to bring to market its Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (LEVI) fund procurement opportunity to deliver additional electric vehicle charging infrastructure (EVCI) in Shropshire.  
The LEVI funding allows large scale deployment of EVCI by the private sector, under contract to Councils, specifically targeting delivery of an equitable charging network. Forecasts indicate that by 2050, EV adoption will be significant, with an estimated 90% of cars being electric (EVs) across both rural and urban areas. The aim of the Government’s LEVI Fund is to get ahead of this demand, ensuring that access to EVCI is not a blocker to the EV transition, particularly for residents who are unable to charge at home. 
The Council’s intention is to appoint a service provider (or consortia) to supply, install, connect and operate the EVCI. The Council will utilise LEVI funds to de-risk delivery for the private sector service provider and support the installation of EVCI to meet the level of demand anticipated for 2035.  
This is an initial market testing exercise to aid the Council in gathering information. It is not an invitation to tender or request formal expressions of interest. A procurement exercise is expected at a future point in 2026, with a view to a service provider being appointed in early 2027 and the first charge points being operational before the end of 2027. It is expected that there will be a 28-week competitive flexible procedure comprising a 4-week premarket engagement phase, a two-stage competition (PSQ and ITT), post tender dialogue , BAFO, final evaluation and moderation , standstill and contract award 
Background to Charging Infrastructure and LEVI in Shropshire   
As of October 2025, there were a total of 546 devices across Shropshire, some of which have been delivered under contract to the Council. Initial analysis indicates that more than 550 new devices can be delivered across the region utilising the LEVI Fund capital funding, doubling the number of devices.  
Work is underway to determine suitable areas and sites for delivery of this scale of EVCI. Devices will be located either on-street or on council owned land in the majority of cases. Further details will be provided at procurement stage. 
Approval was given to take forward the LEVI process at a meeting of the Shropshire Cabinet on 11 March 2026. 
Outline of the Scope of Shropshire Council’s LEVI Scheme 
The anticipated scope of the scheme, in brief, is outlined here: 
The scope of installation will primarily include standard 7kW devices, with the option to incorporate:  
22kW fast devices, where local network capacity and site conditions allow; and  
A limited number of 50kW+ rapid devices, subject to local network capacity and site suitability.  
To facilitate the procurement process, the Council intends to utilise the established documentation available from the LEVI Support body, and available on the NEVIS platform, as far as reasonably possible.  
The service provider will be appointed under a concession contract where the Council grants the service provider the right to deliver, operate, own and maintain EVCI on Council-owned land or highways. A 15-year contract (with the option to extend by one year) is proposed, which is in line with market trends and recommended by the Department for Transport (DfT).  
The Council intends to adopt the Heads of Terms recommendations and will seek an annual concession fee and/or a percentage revenue share which will be determined as part of the procurement process and after undertaking market engagement.  
The Council will invest its £2,006,000 of LEVI Fund capital funding, alongside investment from the service provider. 
Additional Procurement and Scheme Information 
The Council has not finalised its approach to a lotting strategy and is actively considering whether to divide the opportunity into lots or to appoint a single supplier. This decision will be informed by our preferred sites and charging speeds, market engagement and further analysis over the coming months, ensuring that the final structure both attracts strong market support and safeguards the interests of Shropshire’s residents and businesses. 
The Council is updating its EVI Strategy that sets out its vision for the future of EVI and EV transition across the region. This strategy will be made available to bidders.

milestones.description: *PME ONLY* The West Yorkshire Local Authorities and the West Yorkshire Combined Authority (WYCA/CA) require high-quality, robust data on the travel behaviour of residents across West Yorkshire. This evidence is essential to inform policy-making, support the development, appraisal and evaluation of transport strategies and schemes, and to understand the wider impacts of transport investment and policy decisions. West Yorkshire is currently implementing significant transport reforms, including bus franchising, the development of mass transit systems, and broader policies aimed at shifting travel modes, reducing carbon emissions, improving accessibility, and promoting inclusive growth. To effectively design, deliver and evaluate these changes, the Authorities need a detailed understanding of how travel behaviour varies across different groups and how it is evolving over time. In particular, the Authorities need to understand how travel behaviour is changing in response to evolving patterns of employment, land use, population growth, household characteristics and income, as well as changes arising from policy interventions and investment in transport infrastructure. The CA maintains a transport evidence base that combines national and local data sources. This includes a number of recurring surveys that explore travel behaviour, perceptions and satisfaction, such as the Residents’ Perceptions of Transport Survey and the Transport Insights Survey (Please see here for details of the CA’s published surveys: https://www.westyorks-ca.gov.uk/data/surveys/). However, at present, the CA does not collect comprehensive, dedicated data focused solely on detailed travel patterns across West Yorkshire. This project seeks to address that gap. While official datasets such as the National Travel Survey (NTS) collect information on how, why, when and where people travel, and on factors influencing travel behaviour, they do not provide the level of local detail or robustness required to fully support transport planning and evaluation at a West Yorkshire level. The West Yorkshire District Travel Diary Survey (WY TRADS) is aimed to provide a more comprehensive and representative understanding of travel behaviour, including travel patterns, mode choice, accessibility, and distributional impacts. The WY TRADS study is currently planned as a baseline exercise in 2027, with the intention of obtaining baseline data and repeating the survey in future years to enable monitoring of trends over time. The Statement of Requirements (SoR) sets out the objectives of the study, describes the services to be provided by the appointed Consultant, and explains how the study will be managed. The CA, and specifically the Research and Intelligence team, will lead the work in collaboration with the appointed Consultant. The team will ensure that the outputs of the study are usable and relevant for informing future transport policy, assessing the impacts of programmes and projects delivered by the CA, and supporting the work of district authority partners across West Yorkshire. Contract Duration The contract is estimated to start in December 2026 for a term of one year. Preliminary Market Engagement We are inviting prospective Tenderers with interests in providing these services, to attend a 30-minute, individual (one-to-one), virtual Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) sessions with the Research and Intelligence team of the Combined Authority. Kindly respond to this PME Notice to express your interest by 5:00 pm on 5th August 2026. All prospective Tenderers that register for the event shall be invited to a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) event which will be held as follows: Date: 10th – 12th August 2026 Time: To be confirmed through email on 6th – 7th August 2026 Location: Microsoft Teams (a link will be sent to registered Tenderers by 5 pm, two days before their scheduled session). The CA reserves the right to change its procurement approach after the PME. Please respond to this Notice with an expression of interest in this opportunity by accepting the invitation to the PME on YORtender. A draft Statement of Requirements (SoR) is attached with this Notice to provide a general understanding of the requirements of the contract. Please Note: This Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is an invitation only and is not a ‘Call for Competition’. Whilst we encourage your participation in this exercise, failure to respond to the PME will not prohibit your involvement in any future procurement exercise, if progressed via a publicly advertised tender opportunity. Any future opportunity where advertised, will be available through our tender portal at https://yortender.eu-supply.com/ctm/Company/CompanyRegistration/RegisterCompany?OID=9&B=YORTENDER and Consultants are encouraged to register, in readiness for this.

tender.title: Fuel Poverty and Energy Affordability
tender.description:
This project will build on the long-standing approach to delivering trusted, high quality in-person energy support for communities across Devon and Torbay. Through this programme, ECOE Advice will ensure that vulnerable customers continue to receive timely, practical assistance, including carbon monoxide safety guidance and early conversations that support the transition to a net zero future. Support will be delivered through the following ways:
- Home visits.
- Hub drop-ins
- Energy Advice Centres.
- Community events and specialist clinics.
Maintaining leased premises in Exeter and Paignton ensures that accessible, face-to-face support remains available in areas of greatest need. These sites enable customers who do not wish to receive home visits to seek help locally, improve response times and increase the number of households we can support efficiently. 
Alongside face-to-face delivery, the project will provide tailored household support including carbon monoxide safety, Priority Services Register engagement, personalised energy efficiency advice and energy triage. Advisors will also support access to emergency provision, keep-warm resources and onward referrals, including Fire and Rescue Service visits and gas safety interventions where required. 
To maximise the impact of this project, ECOE Advice will recruit four 0.4 FTE roles - a Data Lead a Well in the Home Health Energy Advisor, a People and Culture Lead, and an Income Generation Lead - alongside a 0.2 FTE Fuel Poverty Client Coordinator. 
Benefits include:
- Access to trusted, in-person and community-based energy advice. 
- Improved energy efficiency, reduced fuel poverty and safer, warmer homes. 
- Strengthened referral pathways and faster response times. 
- Better data integration enabling earlier identification of vulnerability. 
- Enhanced financial resilience and improved household wellbeing. 
- Improved physical and mental wellbeing.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
ECOE Advice (Sustainable Community Solutiosn) is a well-established, place-based organisation with specialist expertise in delivering fuel poverty, energy advice and vulnerability support across Devon and Torbay. Through its locally embedded model, ECOE provides trusted, person-centred support that addresses the interconnected challenges of energy affordability, poor housing, health vulnerability and carbon monoxide risk. 
ECOE is uniquely positioned within the region, operating through a strong network of community partners and accessible delivery channels including home visits, Energy Advice Centres, hubs and community outreach. It's model is built on face-to-face, relational engagement, ensuring those most at risk, including digitally excluded and socially isolated households, can access tailored support that is not achievable through remote or standardised approaches. 
This combination of local infrastructure, trusted relationships and integrated delivery cannot be readily replicated without disrupting established pathways, reducing accessibility and weakening engagement with vulnerable households. ECOE plays a critical role in providing consistent, community-based access to support, particularly in rural and off-gas areas where need is high and services are often fragmented.  
The proposed investment represents a continuation and strengthening of this proven model, enabling ECOE to maintain core services while building capacity following its transition to an independent charity. This ensures continuity of support for vulnerable households, protects established delivery capability and avoids fragmentation across the wider Devon support landscape.

lots.title: Technical Consultancy Support

To provide specialist advice and expertise on all aspects of offshore energy & infrastructure, aquaculture and marine ecosystem services areas, to support development function activities for all sectors, enabling activities and provision of technical due diligence.
This work will typically include technical advice notes, reporting, and publications which will be shared by CES or in collaboration with partner organisations, or occasionally for internal CES use.

Each project will have its own specific requirements; however, it should be assumed that all will require provision of project management. lots.title: Commercial & Economic Support
lots.description:

To undertake periodic and as needed sector and/or project specific commercial reviews to inform the terms (e.g. rental) which will be applied to our seabed agreements. The terms require to be applied to each type of agreement (Exclusivity/Appraisal Agreement, Option Agreement, Lease and/or Licence) and offered in ad-hoc leasing and in leasing rounds. These commissions will typically require review of our leasing guidance documents, Heads of Terms, existing and model from agreements and other relevant policies. The specific terms to be considered include (but are not limited to):
Leasing terms
Application fees
Option Fees
Option Periods
Limits on live option agreements at any one time
Lease rental fees and/ or mechanisms
Financial Security and liability requirements
Estimated maximum loss requirements
Insurance requirements
Fee indexing mechanisms (e.g. CPI versus RPI)
Open market rent assessments for operational leases
These reviews will consider the background context within which the particular sector is developing _operating, including:
current market conditions
uncertainties in revenue support or business models
value to the grantee arising from the rights (including in the context of specific project economics)
Regulatory environments and frameworks (eg Ofgem frameworks for Regulated Assets)
Specific to Energy & Infrastructure:
consideration of grid reinforcements and associated grid curtailment payments; subsidy and/ or regulated asset regimes;
and
policy and process developments brought forward by Government and National Energy System Operator (e.g. connections reform).
Specific to Aquaculture:
updates to sea lice framework as result of industry legal challenge to SEPA proposed framework.

tender.description:
The Authority intends to run a Tender process for the provision of RAF Nurseries using Open Competition with Lots. The Tender will be open for 25 Calendar days. The locations will be split into Lots as outlined below:
Lot 1 to include RAF Cranwell, Wellesley Way, Cranwell, Sleaford NG34 8HB.
Lot 2 to include RAF Marham, Elm Road, Upper Marham, King’s Lynn, Norfolk, PE33 9NF.
All suppliers are to submit a response to all evaluation questions (even if not applicable) relating to the Lot/s they wish to bid for. Failure to do so will render your bid non-compliant.
Suppliers can bid for one lot or both lots within the Tender.
For any bids you do not wish to bid for please leave the questions blank.
Description of the procurement:
The below provides a brief illustration of the current provision and operational delivery of the nursery and childcare sites. Please note this is an illustration and detail can be subject to change. There will be scope to work with each station to adapt the operational delivery and outputs of the setting to meet the needs of service families and the station’s statement of requirements. 
RAF Cranwell
The nursery operates out of a purpose-built nursery that is located inside of the wire at RAF Cranwell, Sleaford NG34 8HB. The nursery is currently open Mon – Fri from 07.30 – 18.00 for 51 days of the year providing up to 76 places for children aged 0-5 years, including an offer of full, half day and sessional options to meet the needs of service families living and working at RAF Cranwell. There are currently 92 children under 5 on roll at the nursery. Wraparound childcare and holiday provision for up to 40 places is also offered to children aged 4 – 11 years at other sites within close proximity to the nursery. There are 35 staff employed to work with the children. The nursery provides funded early education for children aged 9months+.
RAF Marham 
The nursery and childcare provision operates out of a purpose built-building facility that is located outside the wire at RAF Marham. The setting is currently open 0700 – 1800 and operates all year round providing up to 186 places at any one time for children aged 0 – 11 years including an offer of full days, part time, sessional and wraparound childcare options to meet the needs of service families. There are 44 staff employed to work with the children. The setting provides funded early education for children aged 9 months+.

The contract is for the procurement of a medium-frequency 300 kHz Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP), capable of fulfilling the requirement of long-term deep-water mooring research.

lots.title: Industrial
lots.description:
This contract was originally tendered under PCR2015 using the Open Procedure in late 2023 for a 4-year contract (Jan 2024 – Dec 2027).  The advertised awarded contract value was £10M.  It was one of 3 gas contracts awarded to BOC Limited by Leidos following 3 failed competitions. The current contract (“the Industrial Gases Contract”) is due to end on 31st December 2027.
The other two contracts awarded to BOC were: (i) The Supply of Medical Gases (“the Medical Gases Contract”) also under PCR, currently due to end also on 31st December 2027, and (ii) the contract for the Supply & Support of Refrigerant Gases, Bulk and Cryospeed Gases & Associated Equipment (“the Refrigerant Gases Contract”) under DSPCR, which is due to end on 31st December 2030.  
Leidos now intends to extend both the Industrial Gases Contract and the Medical Gases Contract for 3 years to make their end dates coterminous with the Refrigerant Gases Contract in 2030 thereby enabling all three to be re-aggregated and let together in the future. Having attempted (unsuccessfully) to disaggregate the three requirements previously in the hope of generating more competition it is now felt that there is more logic in enabling a more consolidated, cost-effective and cohesive single gases tender approach.  
The proposed strategy allows time for further developments in the gases supply markets that could prevent a repeat of the failed tenders at the end of 2023.  
This new approach also eliminates the significant inconvenience and substantial duplication of costs for the contracting authority of running three tenders rather than a single consolidated one.
To facilitate the proposed contract extension, it is proposed to modify the value of the Framework Contract originally awarded to BOC ( original value £10m) to £14.85m on the basis that the provisions of PCR Regulation 72 (Modification of Contracts during their term): 72 (1) (b): apply- i.e.:
 “ …Contracts and framework agreements may be modified without a new procurement procedure ….. for additional works services or supplies by the original contractor that have become necessary and were not included in the initial procurement where a change of contractor:   (i) cannot be made for economic or technical reasons such as requirements of interchangeability or interoperability with existing equipment, services or installations procured under the original procurement and (ii) would cause significant inconvenience or substantial duplication of costs for the contracting authority
..provided that any increase in price does not exceed 50% of the value of the original contract.
Future demand under the extended contract is difficult to determine accurately.
Call offs under the extended framework will be monitored and, if it is anticipated that the revised framework value might be exceeded a further VEAT will be published.

It was one of 3 gas contracts awarded to BOC Limited by Leidos following 3 failed competitions. The current contract (“the Industrial Gases Contract”) is due to end on 31st December 2027.
The other two contracts awarded to BOC were: (i) The Supply of Medical Gases (“the Medical Gases Contract”) also under PCR, currently due to end also on 31st December 2027, and (ii) the contract for the Supply & Support of Refrigerant Gases, Bulk and Cryospeed Gases & Associated Equipment (“the Refrigerant Gases Contract”) under DSPCR, which is due to end on 31st December 2030.  
Leidos now intends to extend both the Industrial Gases Contract and the Medical Gases Contract for 3 years to make their end dates coterminous with the Refrigerant Gases Contract in 2030 thereby enabling all three to be re-aggregated and let together in the future. Having attempted (unsuccessfully) to disaggregate the three requirements previously in the hope of generating more competition it is now felt that there is more logic in enabling a more consolidated, cost-effective and cohesive single gases tender approach.  
The proposed strategy allows time for further developments in the gases supply markets that could prevent a repeat of the failed tenders at the end of 2023.  
This new approach also eliminates the significant inconvenience and substantial duplication of costs for the contracting authority of running three tenders rather than a single consolidated one.
To facilitate the proposed contract extension, it is proposed to modify the value of the Framework Contract originally awarded to BOC ( original value £10m) to £14.85m on the basis that the provisions of PCR Regulation 72 (Modification of Contracts during their term): 72 (1) (b): apply- i.e.:
 “ …Contracts and framework agreements may be modified without a new procurement procedure ….. for additional works services or supplies by the original contractor that have become necessary and were not included in the initial procurement where a change of contractor:   (i) cannot be made for economic or technical reasons such as requirements of interchangeability or interoperability with existing equipment, services or installations procured under the original procurement and (ii) would cause significant inconvenience or substantial duplication of costs for the contracting authority
..provided that any increase in price does not exceed 50% of the value of the original contract.
Future demand under the extended contract is difficult to determine accurately.
Call offs under the extended framework will be monitored and, if it is anticipated that the revised framework value might be exceeded a further VEAT will be published.

If this process fails, a new competitive tender under the Open Procedure will commence and be advertised in the usual manner.
